messages:
josh: heads up — noticed the Usage heatmap hangs for ~2-4s when toggling series on the dashboard in chrome stable. main thread spikes, page unresponsive for a bit.

maria: repro'd it locally. flame chart shows a big chunk inside JSON.parse + string concat. looks like we parse metric payloads on main thread instead of streaming them into the worker. :thinking_face:

devon: curious — did anything change in the chunking/encoding? i remember we landed a small lz4 wasm fallback in the last frontend PR (PR #4211). if wasm fails we use lz4-js sync path.

josh: yep that PR. on canary i see two code paths: worker->wasm decompress, or fetch -> main-thread lz4-js. for some requests we're getting the second path.

maria: i dug a bit — network shows chunked responses with header: `x-compression: lz4` but in ~15% cases worker init rejects with `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming is not a function` (older embed?). fallback is synchronous decode.

paul: telemetry confirms. metric:console.main_thread_block_ms spikes correlate with the lz4-js path. query: `sum(main_thread_block_ms) by (release,route) where header_x_compression=\"lz4\"` shows canary has 3x.

alice: we should roll the wasm in a more defensive way — feature-flag it for canary regions only. also add a fast path that streams into worker if possible. immediate mitigation: revert the lz4-js sync fallback or make it async via setImmediate/messageChannel.

devon: revert is quick. PR #4211 had a small change in bundle that also bumped a dependency which changed tree-shaking; possible the worker blob no longer shipped for some bundles. i'll check the canary bundle content.

josh: timeline: canary started ~1765549000. symptoms first reported by support at ~1765551200. impact is UI jank for dashboard-heavy users. not catastrophic but noisy.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-05-02T08:12Z finished (sha abc123). rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 100% (paused).

maria: quick inspect: worker file missing from two CDN edge nodes — looks like the async chunk name changed, causing some edges to serve older manifest. edge cache mismatch -> clients try to instantiate worker but get 404, then worker init throws and fallback executes.

alice: ok, action plan: 1) pause rollout to remaining regions (devon) 2) hotfix: change fallback to async decode (maria) 3) invalidate CDN for the new worker chunk + ensure manifest consistent (devops) 4) add telemetry to flag worker-init failures (josh/paul).

devon: pausing. putting a hold on the rollout now. also opening a rollback PR to revert the sync-fallback.

paul: i'll add a telemetry counter `worker_init_fail` and a quick alert if it goes above threshold. query snippet i used: `count_over_time(worker_init_fail[5m]) > 10` — will post into #oncall-alerts if it trips.

josh: thanks. after rollback we'll run the dashboard perf canary script against a small user cohort and watch main_thread_block_ms and lcp.

maria: note for follow-up: add a streaming decode path to avoid big JSON.parse spikes. also consider gzip for small chunks rather than lz4 if wasm availability is spotty.

alice: can we also surface a tiny UX hint instead of full freeze? like optimistic toggle then update when data arrives so the UI doesn't lock while parsing. low-risk UX improvement.

josh: agreed. filed a tracking ticket in product board. i'll update thread with rollback + telemetry results.

devon: created rollback PR #4278 and paused canary. please ack in codeowners so i can merge quickly.

paul: alert created, adding watchers. will report if anything else spikes.

josh: quick note for postmortem: root cause appears to be a combination of worker chunk cache mismatch + sync JS fallback for lz4. two weaker links multiplied. we should aim for robust worker loading + safe async fallbacks.

maria: yep — also let's add a simple health-check in the worker bootstrap so we can fail early and route to server-side decode if necessary.

josh: thanks everyone. ping me if you see new reports. :thumbsup:
